text:
maya: Heads-up, ran the multi-GPU perf sweep on the kv-prefetch branch and saw repeated stalls during stage-3 decode. Putting traces here for folks to eyeball.
liam: ugh, still that jitter? can you paste the nsys command you used?
maya: ran:
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,nccl,osrt -o /tmp/run_kv_prefetch_quick /path/to/bin --model x
```
perf-bot: nsys report uploaded: https://perf.internal/runs/1847654321 (nccl timeline + gpu kernels) :white_check_mark:
alejandro: I skimmed the nccl timeline — there's a recurring allreduce bubble between GPU1 and GPU2 around t=11.8s where GPU0 finishes 3ms earlier and waits ~6-8ms.
junaid: can you dump the kernel names for that window? think we had a kernel selection fallback that uses small-block GEMM which regresses for seq_len>1024.
maya: snippet from the nsys call (trimmed):
```
11.804s  GPU0 kernel: matmul_qk_fast 3.1ms
11.806s  GPU1 kernel: matmul_qk_slow 9.6ms
11.816s  NCCL allreduce start (GPU1->GPU0)
11.824s  NCCL allreduce wait on GPU0 for 6.2ms
```

liam: that matmul_qk_slow looks like the non-quantized path. Did the kernel selector flip because of a weird sequence length distribution in that batch?
maya: interestingly, batches on GPU1 had more cache misses during KV lookup (see perf counters). KV prefetcher spawned an async load that increased SM usage before the matmul, maybe evicting L2 and causing the matmul fallback.
alejandro: so chain is: KV prefetch launches on high-prio stream, saturates some SM resources -> matmul on normal stream gets slower -> NCCL allreduce waits -> pipeline bubble.
junaid: sounds plausible. Any differences in CUDA stream priorities set in the runtime? we used default earlier but recent patch added priority=1 to prefetch stream on dedicated nodes.
maya: confirmed: runtime patch sets prefetch stream to high priority on dedicated, low on hosted. This regression only repros on dedicated nodes in the run matrix.
liam: ok that explains why only some runs blow up. Two remediation paths: 1) lower prefetch stream priority or 2) move prefetch to a different SM partition via kernel launch params / cooperative groups. Which is easier short term?
alejandro: quick test: set prefetch to low priority and re-run nsys with nccl debug env to get more precise overlap metrics.
maya: will try now. also attaching the perfetto snippet for the same window (pulled from report):
```
# perfetto selection
track: GPU1 SM utilization: 78% -> spike at 11.8s
track: GPU0 SM utilization: 45% -> matmul short
nccl: allreduce latency: 6.2ms
```

perf-bot: scheduled test job: job/rvw-1847654321-lowprio at 1847654400.
junaid: if low-prio fixes it we may want heuristic: prefetch priority = f(seq_len_mean, kv_hit_rate). low priority when seq_len > 512 or kv_hit_rate < 0.6.
liam: agree. also add a metric to console: "prefetch_priority_effect" that correlates matmul runtime delta with presence of prefetch during preceding 10ms.
maya: quick run result: prefetch set to low priority removed the long matmul on GPU1, allreduce bubble disappears in this sample (nsys out linked).
alejandro: nice. Please open a lightweight PR to revert the priority change on dedicated and add an opt-in config field with default low. We can later implement adaptive heuristic.
maya: filing PR now, will attach traces and the nvprof output.
liam: cool. postmortem next week? or quick prod note? this one can hit latency SLOs so escalate to eng-oncall if it lands in canary. :exclamation:
maya: agreed, pinging eng-oncall once PR is merged.
perf-bot: nvprof snippet saved at /artifacts/1847654321/nvprof_kv_prefetch.txt
maya: thanks — if anyone wants raw counters i dumped L2_misses and sm_efficiency for the window. attaching inline: L2_misses: GPU1=12.3k, GPU0=3.1k; sm_eff: GPU1=42%, GPU0=71%.
junaid: that delta nails it. Good catch. We'll add a unit test that simulates async prefetch overlap and assert matmul kernel selection remains stable.
maya: done for now, will update thread with PR link and canary results.
